### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1 (route, 100 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `26ad5305788a1b0eb1f5f97222b1547c76b0a398` — the merge of head `520df1bfa636cb2595168f4137c8df4fe78dadd5` into base `4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 26ad5305788a1b0eb1f5f97222b1547c76b0a398 && git checkout 26ad5305788a1b0eb1f5f97222b1547c76b0a398
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e 520df1bfa636cb2595168f4137c8df4fe78dadd5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e && git merge --no-ff 520df1bfa636cb2595168f4137c8df4fe78dadd5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4e2c42f363a5f1dc45f2aad01fa05dcd423ac58e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head, latest per name, read twice (15:26Z and 15:33Z):
- NOT COMPLETED at the second read: Test Core (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (5/6), (6/6) — in_progress, NOT MEASURED. Test Core (1/6), Type Check · workspace and Type Check · consumer gates completed `success` between the two reads.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:
1. `GET {base}/docs` on both route shapes stops being served. The only code hunks in discovery-routes.ts are the removed `escapeHtml` import and the removed 51-line registration block; no handler, no catch, no special-cased refusal replaces it, so the answer is whatever the host gives any unmounted path. The report measured 404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND on plugin-hono-server and the node IHttpServer, both shapes, anonymous and signed in, byte-identical to a never-served control, and createHonoApp unchanged at 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND. The new pin holds absence at registrar level on both shapes under all five verbs (getRoutes, routeManager.get, host paths); the dogfood case holds the never-served control's body on a booted showcase for anonymous and member alike and refuses text/html. The ledger holds no base-level parameter route that could swallow the path. RIGHT; nothing new exists to leak, and 404 versus 401 is the host's standing behaviour for every unmounted path.
2. `GET {base}/openapi.json` kept byte-for-byte: the document handler, its registration and the `api.enableOpenApi` gate in `RestServer.registerRoutes` (rest-server.ts:4752) are code-unchanged — the only hunks inside the handler are comments (the servers[0] note). `paths` is produced from `getRoutes()` by `buildBuiltinPaths`, so the one lost path is derived, not hand-edited; the new pin controls that the served 3.1 document still lists its own path on each base and lists no /docs path. The anonymous-deny test's document assertions are unchanged on both bases. RIGHT.
3. `api.enableOpenApi` now gates one route: mount-table pin and dead-keys pin moved to the one route; CASES.length stays 20. RIGHT.
4. `RestServer.getRoutes()` loses one entry per base and the ledger drops `GET /api/v1/docs`: 81 → 80 `route:` and `family:` rows re-counted at the head; the unchanged conformance test holds both directions. RIGHT.

9. 11. The merge of origin/main edcc8ceae6 (#25114 ruling A plus one spec describe commit): the three-dot diff equals the branch's own diff exactly (17 files, +371 / -316), so the merge adds nothing of its own. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25104-rest-docs-viewer-retired.md` declares `'@objectstack/rest': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a BREAKING banner, an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker and a one-line reader migration. Neither the changeset body nor the PR body carries a `Metadata-protocol:` line.

The arm is RIGHT: a published route stops being served and nothing widens.

The level is WRONG at this head. The diff moves nothing a metadata author can write — no spec key, accepted value, type, export, config field or response shape — so its kind is `Metadata-protocol: none`, and under ruling A `none` takes `patch`: "a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and KEEPS its carriers: the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition" (AGENTS.md, the changeset rule; pr-automation.yml "WHICH LEVEL"; check-changeset-no-major.mjs `judgeLevel`). Ruling A landed on main at f2b6cf230b, 2026-10-21T13:08Z — the very commit the claim amendment 6318003983 says its surface was read on — and is present at the merge-base and at this head. The "launch-window convention for breaking changes → minor" the changeset and PR body cite is the 2026-09-04 rule ruling A amended; only its `major` refusal survives. The gate on this head reads it the same way: Check Changeset is `failure`, `not-measured-material` ("a kind and a `none` would grade this differently"); declaring the honest `none` on the changeset as it stands would become `none-minor`, exit 1, and `narrowed` would be a false declaration, since no authorable key or value leaves.

Remedy, a push rather than a body edit alone: grade `'@objectstack/rest': patch`; add `Metadata-protocol: none` as a bare line beside `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset body and in the PR body; keep the BREAKING banner, the `(narrowing)` arm, the ADR-0087 marker and the migration line. That is a new head and owes a new record.

Scope: packages/rest/src/discovery-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/openapi-builtin-paths.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/src/html-escape.ts (deleted), packages/rest/src/html-outlets.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-docs-viewer-retired.pin.test.ts (new), packages/rest/src/rest-api-description-anonymous-deny.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-config-dead-keys-refused.test.ts, packages/rest/src/execctx-consumer-census.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-probe-blind-spot.census.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts (all fourteen byte-identical to head 1379d30df4, judged there by record 6319920291 and carried here by citation) + .changeset/25104-rest-docs-viewer-retired.md (at both heads, and the delta between them), the PR body as it stands, the PR file list, the net diff stat against merge-base edcc8ceae6 and the three-dot diff against origin/main 4e2c42f363, AGENTS.md on origin/main (Post-Task Checklist step 3, lines 1084 to 1101), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml on origin/main (WHICH LEVEL lines 754 to 813; ### ① Derived judgments

**The delta, proven.** `git diff 1379d30df4289aa759c7297d94de51a215b1a12c 520df1bfa636cb2595168f4137c8df4fe78dadd5` touches exactly one path, `.changeset/25104-rest-docs-viewer-retired.md`, +3 / −2: the frontmatter `'@objectstack/rest': minor` becomes `patch`; a line-initial `Metadata-protocol: none` is inserted directly under `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the BREAKING banner's tail changes from "shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention for breaking changes" to "shipped as `patch` because it is a non-protocol change: it changes what a REST caller is served, not what a metadata author can write". The summary line, the adr-0087 HTML-comment marker, the three bullets and the reader migration line are byte-identical. The merge-base against origin/main is still edcc8ceae6, and the net diff is the same 17 files (+372 / −316; the one extra insertion versus the prior record's +371 is the changeset's new line); the three-dot diff against current origin/main 4e2c42f363 reports the identical 17 files and counts, so nothing from `main` entered this head. **Carried by citation.** Because no non-prose path moved between the two heads, record 6319920291's ① judgments 1 to 11 on head 1379d30df4 carry whole to this head: the route retirement on both shapes with the host's own not-found answer (1); `/openapi.json`, its gate and its answer code-unchanged, `paths` derived not hand-edited (2); `api.enableOpenApi` gating one route (3); the ledger 81 to 80 both directions (4); `html-escape.ts` never exported (5); the outlet census kept, positive control on a fixture (6); every dogfood and execctx count re-derived, the floor kept (7); no still-true assertion loosened (8); the ADR anchor against ADR-0076 D12, ADR-0056 D2 and ADR-0138 D2 (9); the packages/spec residue out of this PR by rule, carried by #25121 (10); the merge of main adding nothing (11). ### ② Semver level

Judged afresh against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 on `main` (ruling A, #25114, landed f2b6cf230b at 13:08Z, an ancestor of the merge-base and of this head):

- **`'@objectstack/rest': patch` — RIGHT.** The only published package the diff moves is `@objectstack/rest` (18.0.0, not private); `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`; `docs/qa/**` and `scripts/adr-anchors/**` publish nothing. One entry, and the kind decides its level.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — RIGHT**, unchanged: a published route stops being served and nothing widens (carried ①.1 to ①.3).
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — RIGHT.** Nothing a metadata author can write changes: no key added, removed or tombstoned, no accepted value refused, no requirement tightened, no meaning or default changed, no metadata type; no shard under `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` moves. The one authorable key in reach, `api.enableOpenApi` (rest-server.zod.ts:144, boolean, default true, embedder-only), keeps its accept set, its default and its intent; the route set that switch covers is a runtime fact, which ruling A's table files under `none` ("REST ... `fix!:` alike"), and its describe text still naming the viewer is "description or error text" — also `none`, and #25121's to regenerate. `narrowed` would be false (no key or value leaves) and would anyway be the right kind only for a protocol narrowing; `semantic` would be false (no authorable key's meaning or default moves). Under `judgeLevel` this is `none`, one introduced entry at `patch`, no baseline moved: `none-clean`, exit 0 — the gate's own ruling-A pin is this exact shape (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none` → `none-clean`), and Check Changeset is `success` on the head.
- **The BREAKING banner — kept, and its new wording is TRUE.** The code hunks are the removal of one route registration in `packages/rest` (what a REST caller is served); nothing under `packages/spec/` moves and no authorable key, value, default or type changes (what a metadata author can write).
